name: Shotlist
tagline: Turn your screenshots into sorted ideas, places, recipes and reminders.
status: TestFlight beta (not on the public App Store yet)
about:
Shotlist reads the screenshots in your Screenshots album and sorts each one into a category such as ideas, recipes or places. It writes a short summary and action steps, puts places on a map, and reminds you about things you saved. Your screenshots are analyzed on your phone.

There is no account and no developer server for your content.

collects.what: Screenshots from your Photos "Screenshots" album (read only)
collects.where: They stay in Photos. The app stores only a reference to each one.
collects.shared: Nobody. The one exception is optional tester feedback in beta builds (see below).

collects.what: Text read from each screenshot on your phone, plus the title, summary, steps, tags, category, place name, city and map position, and the source app, handle or link visible in it
Place lookups and city lookups: a place name with a city or state hint, sometimes a search area around you, and your current location when the app works out which city you are in
collects.shared: Apple Maps and Apple location services
collects.why: To find a place and show it on the map, and to know your current city for suggestions and arrival reminders.

collects.what: Your location, including "Always" if you allow it, and areas around your saved places
collects.shared: Apple only receives the place-search area and the location used to look up your city (above). Nobody else.
collects.why: For "near me" suggestions and for reminders when you arrive in a new city or near a saved place.

collects.what: Links you share into Shotlist, and any text shared with them
collects.shared: Nobody. Shotlist does not open the web page; it saves the link and the text shared with it.
collects.why: To save the link as an item.

collects.what: Activity log (details in the diagnostic section below)
A "Send to support" report: Help-chat text, self-check results, masked log lines and device info (about 4 KB)
collects.where: Held on your phone until you send it
collects.shared: Only if you tap Send. It is encrypted and sent through a free public relay (ntfy.sh) to the developer.
collects.why: So the developer can help you.

collects.what: Tester feedback (thumbs up or down): what the sorter produced, up to 3,000 characters of the text read from the screenshot, and optionally a JPEG of the screenshot itself. It is sent only when you tap to send it.
collects.where: A feedback file on your phone
collects.shared: Sent to the developer through the same encrypted relay. In TestFlight and debug builds the feedback buttons and "Include the screenshot" are on by default, so a screenshot can be sent with your feedback. You can switch both off in Settings.
collects.why: To improve the sorter. This is planned to be turned off before a public release.

collects.what: "Flag this" report (developer's own test devices only): a note, an outlined spot, a screenshot of the app screen and the last 30 seconds of masked log
collects.where: Built into TestFlight and debug builds only; it is off unless the developer switches it on
collects.shared: Sent to the developer through the same encrypted relay, only when sent

collects.where: On your phone; the last 14 backups are kept
collects.shared: Nobody, unless you share a file

usage_data:
Shotlist keeps an activity log on your phone. It writes a short line every 10 seconds, even when idle. It also records events such as scans, notifications, shared links and place searches. Some of these lines can include a link you shared or the place text that was searched.

The log is kept for 30 days and capped at about 1 GB. It is never uploaded automatically. You can view and export it in Settings, under Logs. It leaves your phone only if you export it yourself, or if you send a support report, tester feedback or a Flag this report, which include a few masked log lines.
not_collected: No developer server for your screenshots or content
No upload of the activity log
No iCloud sync, contacts, camera, microphone or health data

third_parties.what: Apple Maps and location services get a place name with a city or state hint, sometimes a search area, and your coordinates when the app looks up your current city. Apple also provides Photos, Siri, Spotlight and notifications.
An encrypted support report or tester feedback, only when you send it. The developer holds the key to read it.

permissions.name: Photos
permissions.why: To read only your Screenshots album so Shotlist can sort screenshots and make action plans.

permissions.name: Location (while using the app)
permissions.why: To suggest places you screenshotted that are near you.

permissions.name: Location (Always)
permissions.why: To notice when you arrive somewhere new, like another city, and remind you about places you saved there.

permissions.name: Notifications
permissions.why: For occasional reminders and nearby-place alerts.

permissions.name: Live Activities and background updates
permissions.why: To show scan progress and scan screenshots in the background.

permissions.name: Siri and Shortcuts
permissions.why: So you can ask for suggestions by voice, such as "I'm bored", and so Siri and Spotlight can find and tell you about items you saved. This uses on-phone indexing.

retention:
Logs are kept 30 days. The last 14 backups are kept. If you pick a folder in Files for backup copies, those copies stay there until you delete them.

To clear the app, open Settings and choose Erase All Data. It deletes your items, scan runs and categories, then clears settings, logs, on-phone backups, tester feedback and waiting queues. It shows an error if anything could not be erased. It does not touch your Photos, other devices, or backup copies you put in a folder you chose. "Forget" removes a single item. Pausing stops the app from reading new screenshots. Deleting the app removes its data from your phone.

A support report or tester feedback you already sent cannot be taken back.
children: Shotlist is not directed at children. It has no accounts, and the developer does not knowingly collect data from children.
support_what: Shotlist helps you do something with the screenshots you take. It sorts them, summarizes them, finds places on a map and reminds you. It works on your phone, with no account.
support_steps: Open Shotlist and allow access to your Screenshots album when asked.
Wait for the first scan to finish. A Live Activity shows its progress.
Browse your categories, or search for something you saved.
Allow location and notifications if you want place suggestions and reminders.
To save a link, use the Share button in another app and choose Shotlist. It saves the link and any text shared with it.

support_faq.a: No. Screenshots are analyzed on your phone. The exception is beta builds from TestFlight: if you give thumbs-up or thumbs-down feedback, the app can send the sorter's result and, by default, the screenshot to the developer. You can switch this off in Settings, and the developer plans to remove it before a public release.

support_faq.q: Why does it ask for Always location?
support_faq.a: Only to notice when you arrive in a new city and remind you about places you saved there. You can use the app with While Using the App or with no location.

support_faq.q: How do I remove one item?
support_faq.a: Use Forget on the item. To remove everything, use Erase All Data in Settings.

support_faq.q: Where can I see the activity log?
support_faq.a: In Settings, under Logs. You can export it from there.

support_faq.q: Can I stop it reading new screenshots?
Does Shotlist open the links I share?
support_faq.a: No. It saves the link and the text shared with it, and does not load the web page.

support_faq.q: Something went wrong. How do I get help?
support_faq.a: Open Help (on the welcome screen or in Settings) and tap Send to support. Nothing is sent until you tap it.
